replies.text:
Check of commonly-missed items:

1. Automated abuse / scraping / flooding — design has an endpoint returning bulk data: "Account admins call POST /exports to export all users in their organisation as CSV" — covered by listed threats 3 (repeated export DoS) and 5 (bulk PII pull).
2. Staff/admin screens rendering user-supplied content — the admin opens an export containing user-controlled profile fields: "including names, email addresses and phone numbers" — covered by listed threat 4 (formula injection executing in the admin's spreadsheet).
3. Privileged actions with no record — design describes no logging of exports: "Account admins call POST /exports" — covered by listed threat 6 (no record of who exported which organisation's data).
4. Personal documents cacheable by browsers/proxies/CDNs — the design names only a POST endpoint and no download URL, storage location, cache or CDN: "The organisation id comes from the request body." Nothing in the design states a cacheable GET/download exposure, so reporting this would depend on how it is built — not reported.
5. Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, exports, emails or headers — present only as the CSV path, which is covered by listed threat 4; no logging, email or header sink is stated in the design — not covered by a new threat because the design does not state such a sink.

Single-reviewer threats: none provided.

Conclusion: the agreed list already covers every threat the design text supports.
